text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Vukovar city council was established late on Wednesday. Vladimir Stengl, a ruling party member, is elected mayor.
- Croatian number plates to appear in Eastern Slavonia on Monday.

- Following its successful rehabilitation, Rijecka Banka is to get its first 25 million German mark loan from Munich-based Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale. An agreement on this to be signed on June 2 in Munich.
- International Crafts Fair to be held in Zagreb between June 11 - 15.

- A Vecernji list poll suggests among other things that 55.3 percent of those surveyed believe the past seven-year period of Croatia's independence to have been successful, while 57.3 percent think the general situation in Croatia will improve in the future.
- Croatian pop stars to take part in a big "Be smart, don't start" anti-drugs concert scheduled for June 2 in Zagreb.
- Presidential candidate Vlado Gotovac claims only Franjo Tudjman is enjoying favourable conditions in the presidential campaign.

- Tesla telecommunications company does not seem to be making any progress since being sold to the Swedish company Ericsson two years ago. Lay-offs have been announced and production is said to be down. -- Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
